A reversed step can turn a hidden reward into 65–69 gold. The same game builds its landscapes from two-by-two character tiles.

01 · Hidden rewards

The reversal is checked when the reward appears

The game compares two consecutive direction samples as it creates a reward. Try the combinations below.

The two reward entity types run the check at $5C0C. A qualifying reversal stores $FF. On collection, $771F adds an offset from 0 to 4 in decimal mode; the result is $65–$69. Controlled VICE tests cover the direction check and all five additions. The natural pickup was not part of those tests.

The check uses the samples around the creation of the reward, not a measured number of frames before its collection. The code chooses the small random offset when the reward is collected.

02 · Terrain

One map byte becomes four characters

A map cell selects a top-left, top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right character. The game writes those four characters into a two-by-two block and looks up a colour for each.

Explore the captured maps →

The draw loop begins at $6D41; the four character tables begin at $81CF. The map viewer draws terrain from 31 forced load captures, which do not demonstrate routes through ordinary play.

03 · Equipment

The wing boots count qualifying updates

The boots start with a counter of 255. When up is held and the fall-step value is below 4, the game decreases the counter and sets the fall step to 1. At zero it clears the boots flag and selects “Lost the Wing Boots.”

The setup is at $76FD and the update is at $0A92. Five controlled VICE cases checked the branches and expiry flag. The elapsed time depends on how often that code runs.

The Gauntlet lasts ten contacts

The Gauntlet doubles the attack damage for ten successful contacts. The tenth contact still gets double damage; then the game selects “Gauntlet is broken.” The next contact uses ordinary damage.

The pickup sets the counter at $76E9; the contact routine decrements it at $74A9. A controlled VICE sequence checked eleven contacts with the overlap and message callbacks stubbed.

Sound

The game's tunes

Choose a captured load or a built-in sequence to hear its SID writes.

The recordings hold ordered writes made by the game's sequencer at $2201, run ahead of time on the kit's 6502. The player sends those writes to the site's SID model. VICE matched the sequencer state and final SID registers for 50 calls, and the ordered writes for 10 calls, in a controlled load-2 test. It also matched the first 10 calls of each built-in sequence. The captured load states were reached by forced transitions, which do not demonstrate their natural routes. Sequence 3 is silent in the tested state.
